Water level (m, MSL)

Model free surface vs CO-OPS observed water level on the MSL datum. The model is forced by tides + atmospheric pressure/wind, so the tidal band should track closely once the 2026-09-03 tide-forcing phase fix is in (cycles run before it still carry a ~half-M2-period phase error). Model zeta has a fixed +0.64 m datum offset applied (report.zeta_msl_offset_m) to bring its reference level onto the MSL datum; any bias left below is the part that offset does not remove. Low-frequency scatter is non-tidal surge from outside the domain that the boundary forcing under-represents. The first 24 h (RAMP_TIDES spin-up) are excluded. tools/verify_tide_phase.py does the same comparison per constituent against tidal predictions.

Surface current — eastward component (m/s)

Currents here are tide-dominated (tidal signal ~5-10x the residual). Two known limits on this comparison: (1) a tidal-forcing phase error (raw Greenwich phases in tide.nc were not referenced to zero_phase_date) was corrected 2026-09-03 -- cycles run before that still carry it; and (2) history output is 3-hourly (~4 samples per M2 cycle). The first 24 h of each forecast (RAMP_TIDES spin-up) are excluded here. Read the residual/subtidal trend and the component biases rather than the instantaneous tidal-band R.
